section_1_findings.verdict: The three image drivers and ECDHCrypto are not enabled by the business and no request, configuration value or runtime path can switch them on. Every repo-owned hit is one of the accounted construction sites, and the remaining hits are inside the owned upstream package where the driver switch necessarily lives.

captcha_v0.0.4.consequence: this is a production-code gap in the locked upstream implementation, not a missing test asset. Making it work would mean setting driver resources in the implementation, which section 3 forbids, and injecting a configured object into the private driver fields and claiming the default NewCaptcha is fixed is explicitly out of bounds
captcha_v0.0.4.initClickCaptcha: captcha.go:305-343 sets chars only (a hardcoded Chinese alphabet when the config has none); no font resource is registered, so the library reaches freetype DrawText with a nil font
captcha_v0.0.4.initRotateCaptcha: captcha.go:412-424 calls rotate.NewBuilder() with no resource at all and comments that rotate 'uses built-in default images', which v2.0.5 does not provide, so it fails with 'no image'
captcha_v0.0.4.initSlideCaptcha: captcha.go:59-87 gives the builder a background only, and that background is a hand-painted 300x220 gradient produced by loadDefaultBackground (captcha.go:91), not a puzzle/tile image; the tile and range-graph resources go-captcha's slide generator requires are never set, so Generate() fails inside the library with 'graph image is invalid'

password_v0.0.2.DeriveSharedSecret: ecdsa_ecdh.go:124-140 base64-decodes a bare public key (no ecdh$ prefix), unmarshals it and returns sharedX.Bytes()
password_v0.0.2.Encrypt: ecdsa_ecdh.go:87-95 ignores the plaintext apart from the empty check and returns 'ecdh$' + base64(elliptic.Marshal(pubX, pubY)) - it outputs the public key
password_v0.0.2.Verify: ecdsa_ecdh.go:97-121 parses the peer key out of the envelope, computes sharedX = ScalarMult(peerPub, priv.D), and compares sha256(sharedX.Bytes()) with sha256([]byte(plainPassword))
password_v0.0.2.consequence: two different instances can absolutely agree, because both derive the same x-coordinate; the shipped test failed only because it passed the literal string 'test message' as the secret. Rewriting the test to use one instance, or flipping the expected true to false, would hide the contract instead of testing it
